title: Clipboard: decide which formats a copied selection puts on the clipboard
instructions:
Add src/shared/clip-plan.js exporting clipPlan(sel). Today copying in StudyNotes puts only text plus an invisible
marker on the system clipboard, so pasting into another program shows that marker instead of a picture. The app will
write several formats at once; this pure function decides what. Input: { items: [{ type: 'img'|'stroke'|'shape'|'text'|'table',
w, h, text?, natural?: { w, h } }], bbox: { w, h } (page units), zoom (screen pixels per unit) }. Output:
{ png: { mode: 'original' } | { mode: 'render', width, height, scale } | null, text: string, html: boolean, privateClip: true }.
Rules: a selection that is exactly one picture -> mode 'original' (its own bytes, no quality loss). Otherwise render at 2x
screen size (bbox * zoom * 2), but the longer side at most 4000 px (scale down evenly, round to whole pixels, at least 1).
text = the texts of text boxes and table cells in reading order (top to bottom, then left to right; items carry x, y),
joined with newlines, '' when none. html = true when there is a png and text is not empty. An empty selection returns
png null and text ''. Add test/unit/shared/clip-plan.test.js covering every rule, including the 4000 px limit and a
tall thin selection. title: Scroll and zoom: frame-rate independent zoom easing and wheel input
instructions:
Background: scrolling and zooming in StudyNotes lag on long PDFs. Today the viewer (src/renderer/viewer.js, not readable for you) eases zoom with a fixed factor per animation frame (zoom *= (target/zoom)^0.32 each frame), so the speed depends on the screen's frame rate; it re-renders PDF pages sharply 160 ms after zooming stops and keeps rendered pages in a least-recently-used cache limited to 28 million pixels; zoom range 0.1 to 8. Add src/shared/zoom-motion.js. (1) easeZoom(current, target, dtMs, tauMs = 60): the next zoom after dtMs milliseconds,
moving geometrically (in log space) towards target so that the remaining log distance shrinks by exp(-dt/tau); returns
target when the remaining ratio is within 0.4 %. Same result whether a 120 ms move is done in 2, 8 or 15 steps (within
1e-9 in log space). dtMs is clamped to 0..100 (a stalled tab must not jump). (2) wheelZoomFactor({ deltaY, deltaMode,
ctrlKey }): factor for one wheel event: deltaMode 1 (lines) exp(-deltaY * 0.05), pixels exp(-deltaY * 0.0025), the result
clamped to 0.5..2 per event. (3) isTouchpadPinch(e): true for pixel-mode events with |deltaY| < 40 (pinches send many tiny
